commands.label: Switch tab
commands.description: Lists open tabs, most recently used first, and switches to the one you pick.
examples: SPC b b, type user → switches to the open UserService tab
commands.rationale: VSpaceCode and Doom Emacs use SPC b b to switch buffers.

commands.label: Close tab
commands.description: Closes the current tab; the split stays open.
examples: SPC b d → the tab closes; SPC b u brings it back
commands.rationale: VSpaceCode, Doom Emacs and LazyVim all use SPC b d to close a buffer.

commands.label: Close other tabs
commands.description: Closes every other tab in the current split.
examples: Five tabs in one split: SPC b o → only the current tab is left
commands.rationale: Tab commands live under SPC b; LazyVim uses SPC b o (Doom Emacs SPC b O, VSpaceCode SPC b M).

commands.label: Reopen closed tab
commands.description: Reopens the tab you closed most recently.
examples: Closed a tab by mistake: SPC b u → it is open again
commands.rationale: VSpaceCode uses SPC b u to reopen a closed buffer; it pairs with SPC b d.

commands.label: Go to next tab
commands.description: Moves to the next tab in the current split, like gt.
examples: SPC b n → the tab to the right becomes active
commands.rationale: VSpaceCode and Doom Emacs use SPC b n for the next buffer; like gt, it moves only among the tabs of one split.

commands.label: Go to previous tab
commands.description: Moves to the previous tab in the current split, like gT.
examples: SPC b p → the tab to the left becomes active
commands.rationale: VSpaceCode and Doom Emacs use SPC b p for the previous buffer; like gT, it moves only among the tabs of one split.
